description: Reference manifest of the M-SM campaign (m-sm/PLAN.md §4.2), written by tools/loop_reference/mqcd_campaign.py manifest from msm_campaign.json and the committed fixtures. Per row: process, pyAmpliCol route (restriction, fixed parameters), reference runs (fixture path below tests/fixtures/loop, orders, points, MadLoop return codes, evaluation precision and accuracy per point and loop squared split order, rule 1 outliers), existing references (per point binding or superseded) and binding_references: the one binding reference of every point. 'pending' marks a reference not committed yet. Parameters, per-point reference records and per-helicity rows are the fixtures' own (the pyAmpliCol request uses the fixture's parameters and fixed_parameters, the MadLoop card values).

conventions.laurent: MadLoop/BLHA C_eps = (4 pi)^eps / Gamma(1 - eps); physical couplings; initial spin/colour average and final identical-particle factor included
conventions.squared_split_orders: QCD^2, QED^2 = summed g_s and e powers of the interfering amplitudes; a loop sector's born_sector is its orders minus the correction step
conventions.binding_references: per row, the fixtures and rows (0-based) that are the row's rule 1 reference: every ok row of the campaign runs, and the rows of an existing reference that no campaign run re-evaluates ('rows' None: an existing control fixture, not a provider merge, whose own format names its points). An existing reference's point_binding names, per point, the run row superseding it (the same exact point and mu_R, MadLoop's quadruple-precision stage, an ok record) with the strict relative deviation |a - b| / max(|a|, |b|) of its values from the superseding ones; a superseded point is no reference (its accuracy is not listed), while its other providers' values stay the second-provider values of rule 1 (ii) at that point
conventions.evaluation_precision: MadLoop's arithmetic per point from its return code 100 H + 10 T + U: H = 1, 2 double, 3 quadruple, 4 quadruple whose stability test failed (only at points with status 'none' or a declared outlier); None where the fixture keeps no code
conventions.madloop_accuracy: MadLoop's own ACC(i) of SLOOPMATRIX_THRES per point and loop squared split order: ONE number over the three Laurent coefficients (madloop_settings.madloop_accuracy_definition), not a per-coefficient relative accuracy. At double-precision points it is the binary64 estimate, which does not bound a cancelling coefficient (required/uux_uux.json point 1: 0.0 with a single pole 1.2e-12 off the quadruple-precision value). In the quadruple-precision evaluation 0.0 means its two quadruple-precision evaluations (propagators in original and reversed order) printed identical binary64 values for all three coefficients; that test does not see an error both share: against mq-validate's double-double values MadLoop quadruple-precision points with accuracy 0.0 differ by up to ~3.6e-13 (e.g. E01 point 1, B03 point 1 with Ninja 3.4e-13) and by 3.5e-12 or more at the g g > u u~ u u~ outliers, so an accuracy of 0.0 never satisfies rule 1 (i) and every rule 1 failure at such a point is an outlier needing a ruling
conventions.outliers: per reference run, the rule 1 reference outliers (m-qcd/PLAN.md §1.4: the manifest names every one), keyed by 0-based row: the fixture's reference.outlier record (rule, ruling, the state of conditions i and ii, provider evidence)
conventions.second_provider_outcome: per triggered second provider and point: the strict relative difference |a - b| / max(|a|, |b|) of each coefficient from MadLoop's (the outcome of the §4.1 trigger named in second_provider_trigger)
conventions.helicity_reference: the fixture holding the row's per-helicity rows (per_helicity, with a reference record per entry: 'absolute' against the point's summed |Born| only for a vanishing helicity, else 'relative'; status 'none' with a reason where an entry is not a reference)
conventions.per_helicity: MadLoop SLOOPMATRIXHEL_THRES: colour average and identical-particle factor, no helicity average; HelConfigs.dat helicity labels
conventions.indexing: rows, points, mu_r, point_labels, binding rows, point_binding, evaluation_precision, provider_accuracy_per_sector and madloop_return_codes are aligned lists (row i = point i, 0-based); reference_notes, outliers and point_status keys are 0-based row indices; scale_variation's point and copy_of_point are 1-based point numbers (mqcd_campaign.py run --point), its row and copy_of_row the 0-based rows

point_reference.status: 'ok': the row is a reference; 'none': no usable provider reference at this point (reason given), validate it by internal oracles only
point_reference.outlier: None, or a declared rule 1 reference outlier of an ok row (rule, ruling, conditions, providers)
point_reference.comparison: 'relative': compare per coefficient relative to the reference value; 'absolute': a Born-zero point (§4.1 S3), compare |value - reference| against the tolerance times absolute_scale = |Born| at row absolute_scale_row (the nearest regular point) for the Born, and times absolute_scale alpha/(2 pi) (F_s of §1.4) for the Laurent coefficients, never dividing by the vanishing Born
point_reference.born_source: which value the row's (and its sectors') 'born' is: 'madloop' = MadLoop's printed Born; 'madloop_double_pole_over_universal_factor' = at madloop_qp_point points, MadLoop's printed Born is its double-precision Born at the binary64 rounding of the point, not at the published point, so the reference Born is its quadruple-precision double pole over universal_double_pole_factor (the printed value is kept as born_madloop_binary64_input / born_binary64_input)
point_reference.madloop_point: the point MadLoop's loop values refer to: the published point (quadruple precision at a madloop_qp_point point), the binary64 rounding of the published point (double precision), or MadLoop's quadruple-precision repair of that rounding (~1e-16 from an exact published point)
point_reference.born_double_pole_relative_mismatch: MadLoop's printed Born (double precision at the binary64 input) against the Born its quadruple-precision double pole implies. At a regular point both are the same Born to its binary64 rounding (<= 1.1e-13 over the campaign): a larger mismatch is a loop defect of the reference, not point sensitivity (C01 point 1 of batch 2: 4.8e-13 from MadLoop's helicity filter, Recola's own relation holding to 1e-15); at madloop_qp_point points (S1-S3) it is the binary64 condition of the limit point, bounded by the family's stated bound
point_reference.max_sector_double_pole_relative_error: largest violation of the universal double pole over the loop squared split orders (MadLoop's printed values, relative to the point's largest double pole; references.sector_pole_error); the merge refuses ok points above its tolerance, the integrity tests recompute it from the sector values and refuse ok regular points above max(10 x MadLoop's largest sector accuracy, 2e-13) unless the point is a declared outlier. At madloop_qp_point points the reference Born is the double pole over the factor, so the relation holds there by construction for every sector with a Born partner; born_double_pole_relative_mismatch is the falsifiable quantity

conventions.fixture_tolerance: 'tolerance' and 'validation_status' are the references.py merge's provider-agreement check (the G1 2e-8 tolerance); they are not M-SM acceptance values: m-sm/PLAN.md §1.4 applies, with each point's 'reference' record

evaluation.description: as the M-QCD campaign (mqcd_campaign.json): every point in MadLoop's quadruple-precision stage (double-precision acceptance bypassed in the run's loop_matrix.f copy), its own test at MLStabThres 1e-13 choosing Ninja or CutTools, HelicityFilterLevel = 0; CMS exports carry the quadruple-precision model-function repair (MP_RECMS and the other CMPLX calls with KIND=16, references.fix_qp_model_functions)
evaluation.reason: stricter than the accurate mode of m-sm/PLAN.md §4.1 (1e-11, forced test, QP rescue), never looser; the M-QCD campaign's reasons apply

madloop_settings.madloop_accuracy_definition: MadLoop's own accuracy is ONE number per squared split order over the three Laurent coefficients (see mqcd_campaign.json)
madloop_settings.orders: explicit squared orders on every job: QCD^2<=99 QED^2<=99 on joint [virt=QCD QED] requests (MadLoop's default selection drops the highest-alpha sector of mixed-Born requests), == on the sector-only jobs; every squared split order is printed (SECTORS)
